source_snapshot.items: Test connections between FPGA1 and HMC I2C-2
source_snapshot.procedure: Log into HMC and run `i2ctransfer -y 3 w2@0x11 0x04 0x00 r3`; refer to PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Only generic result/photo and unexpected-log checks; no device identity, register meaning or expected reply.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; incorrectly replaces the remote HMC transaction with physical probing/soldering.

source_snapshot.items_direct_xlsx: Test connections between FPGA 1 and HMC I2C-2
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: "【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Log into the HMC and run the following command and ensure you get a reply. Refer to PID : 1114953 for other devices expected on the bus. i2ctransfer -y 3 w2@0x11 0x04 0x00 r3
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: NO | -- not runnable by agent: testing the physical I2C connection/link between the named components (FPGA 1 and HMC I2C-2) is a hardware-integrity check that requires probing/soldering the actual I2C traces and collecting photos per the criteria; the agent cannot touch the hardware or take photos over SSH.

test_case.test_name: Test connections between FPGA 1 and HMC I2C-2 — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify functional communication from HMC I2C-2 to FPGA1 through the correct HMC bus3 path by reading the approved FPGA register and validating its three-byte response.
required_package: PID1114953 mapping of HMC I2C-2 to HMC Linux bus3 and FPGA1 address0x11
FPGA1 device identity and vendor definition for register0x0400
Expected three-byte value/field masks by FPGA1 firmware/version
Proof the write phase only sets a read pointer and is non-mutating
HMC bus3 owner/driver and exclusive-access policy
Timeout/NACK/retry acceptance, HMC/FPGA error counters and recovery
test_case.test_command: Map HMC I2C-2 to Linux bus3, identify0x11 as FPGA1 and register0x0400 as a safe query; collect bus owner and HMC/FPGA error baseline; issue one bounded combined pointer-write/read; decode the three bytes against the FPGA specification; correlate HMC I2C-2/FPGA1 telemetry and ensure no new errors.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."

Confirm physical probing/photos are not core acceptance unless separately scoped.
safety_gate: Verify bus3 and0x11 identity before access
Confirm0x0400 combined transaction is a read-only operation for this FPGA revision
Do not bypass an owning driver or perform concurrent raw transfers
Use one bounded request and capture first failure without automatic retry
Stop on wrong length/value, NACK, timeout, arbitration loss, stuck bus or HMC/FPGA degradation
expected_evidence: PID map proving HMC I2C-2-to-bus3 and FPGA1-at0x11
HMC/FPGA1 identities, firmware, bus owner/driver and pre-health baseline
Vendor register0x0400 definition and expected three-byte matrix
Timestamped exact transaction, stdout/stderr, exit code, latency and decoded fields
Pre/post HMC I2C and FPGA error/status counters without automatic-retry masking
Post-read HMC/FPGA health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Wistron I2C policy assigns this to HMC/platform-management scope and requires controller/bus/address, vendor protocol, expected response and recovery before raw access.

source_conflict.reason: The source does not map HMC I2C-2 to bus3, identify0x11/register0x0400, or define the three-byte expected result. Prior reviews additionally invent physical probing; duplicate code at row155 creates an identity hazard handled by the variant.
